tension: Every swarm result on disk was measured at n_seeds=1, and the harness's own success field is defined as n_positive >= max(1, len(reps)-1) -- which at one seed reads 1 >= 1, i.e. trivially true. So `confirmed: true` in swarm-fd and swarm-fd2 was never evidence of anything: swarm-fd went further and had its threshold edited by hand from max(2,len-1) to max(1,len-1) to flip that field, voiding its own signature (see its amendment.json; the bundle still verifies as invalid and is not citable). The open question is therefore not whether the bias amplifies -- it is whether ANY of the three single-seed observations replicate once the threshold is not self-satisfying. Six independent seeds with a 5-of-6 requirement is the smallest design in which 'replicates' has content and the sign test can actually reject p=0.5 (2*0.5^6 = 0.031 < 0.05). Answering it decides whether the scaling claim goes into a paper at all or becomes a documented non-replication.

power.endpoint: sign test over 6 independent seeds (required_n() models a paired proportion difference, which is not this design; the gate checks required_n_signtest(0.05)=6 instead)
